title: Old Rules in the Site
subtitle: 法律规则 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）
meta: 主题语境：法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）　|　核心词汇：must　|　正文 303 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 must 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1970 nobody in the site ① must hand in the accounts by noon, and every assistant there remembered the fact for years. Three months on the world had turned over: by then even the youngest assistant ② must hand in the accounts by noon without complaint, and nobody troubled to watch. My uncle wrote the change into the plan at once, and read the line aloud once every month thereafter.

The rules, though, were older than either of those worlds. A visitor ③ must not hand in the accounts by noon before the October rains; the builder ④ must not hand in the accounts by noon either, and said so plainly to anybody who asked. Nobody in the site ever thought of arguing with him about it.

⑤ Must anybody hand in the accounts by noon, my uncle wanted to know, without the builder standing beside them? My mother, who heard every version of the story, said we ⑥ must hand in the accounts by noon once the plan was signed and not a day before. Even the oldest assistant agreed with her in the end.

By 1976 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the plan: the work ⑦ must be read before the October fair, and nothing was said otherwise. My uncle swore it ⑧ must have been read long before anybody thought to ask. Must it truly have been read so early? Nobody there could say.

⑨ In 1980 only one person in the whole site must hand in the accounts by noon without help, and my mother kept the name in the plan for thirty years. ⑩ Even today a stranger must not hand in the accounts by noon without permission, and that, my mother said in 1982, is what the old rule was really about. She repeated the sentence whenever the site forgot itself.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. modal. 必须（过去形式 must hand in the accounts by noon：1970 年那时候人人如此）
B. modal. 必须（现在形式 must hand in the accounts by noon：如今连最小的帮工也毫无怨言地做得到）
C. modal. 一定（推测）（现在形式的否定 must not hand in the accounts by noon：规矩不许，如今也仍然如此）
D. modal. 必须（过去形式的否定 must not hand in the accounts by noon：那时的施工员也不能这么做）
E. modal. 必须（疑问句 must anybody hand in the accounts by noon?：叔叔当年追问的话）
F. modal. 必须（间接引语 she said we must hand in the accounts by noon：转述母亲的话）
G. modal. 必须（被动 must be read：活儿被 read 才算办妥）
H. modal. 必须（完成式 must have been read：对早先情形的推断）

items.q: must hand in the accounts by noon
must hand in the accounts by noon without complaint
must not hand in the accounts by noon before
must not hand in the accounts by noon
must anybody hand in the accounts by noon,
we must hand in the accounts by noon once
must hand in the accounts by noon without help
must not hand in the accounts by noon without permission

answers.why: must 表必须，1970 年工地里没有一个人午前交上那些账目，叙述过去的事，故用过去形式 must。
must 表必须，多年之后连最年轻的帮工都毫无怨言地午前交上那些账目，说现在的情况，用 must。
must 表一定（推测），规矩上说客人不得午前交上那些账目，否定形式是 must not hand in the accounts by noon。
must 表必须，施工员当年也不能这么做，过去形式的否定是 must not hand in the accounts by noon。
must 表必须，叔叔追问的是“难道没有人能午前交上那些账目吗”，疑问句 must anybody hand in the accounts by noon?
must 表必须，母亲说的是“簿子签过之后我们才午前交上那些账目”，间接引语里用 must。
must 表必须，施工图上那行字是说活儿必须在集前被人 read，被动形式 must be read。
must 表必须，叔叔断定活儿老早就被 read，对过去的推断用 must have been read。
must 表必须，1980 年只有一个人无人相助也能午前交上那些账目，用过去形式 must。
must 表一定（推测），母亲 1982 年说，如今生人没有许可仍不得午前交上那些账目，否定 must not hand in the accounts by noon。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1970 年，工地里没有一个人午前交上那些账目，人人都把这件事记了好多年。（must hand in the accounts by noon）
多年以后，连最年轻的帮工都毫无怨言地午前交上那些账目。（must hand in the accounts by noon）
按老规矩，客人在十月雨季之前不得午前交上那些账目。（must not hand in the accounts by noon）
那位施工员当年也不能午前交上那些账目，谁问他就直说。（must not hand in the accounts by noon）
母亲说，簿子签过之后我们才可以午前交上那些账目，早一天也不行。（she said we must hand in the accounts by noon）
叔叔一口咬定，那件活儿早在有人过问之前就被 read 了。（must have been read）
answers: In 1970 nobody in the site must hand in the accounts by noon, and every assistant there remembered the fact for years.
Three months on, even the youngest assistant must hand in the accounts by noon without complaint.
A visitor must not hand in the accounts by noon before the October rains.
The builder must not hand in the accounts by noon either, and said so plainly to anybody who asked.
My mother said we must hand in the accounts by noon once the plan was signed and not a day before.
My uncle swore that it must have been read long before anybody thought to ask.
